ISSUE #000•ELECTROMECHANICAL•13 MIN READ

Apple Vision Pro: Automatic Lens Adjustment & Voice Coil Motors

How magnetic actuators and optical linear encoders automatically align lenses to your eyes to prevent motion sickness.

1. The Biomechanical Imperative: Human Anatomical Variance & Why Manual IPD Fails

In high-resolution spatial computing, optical alignment is the fundamental physics gating factor for stereoscopic image fusion, binocular depth perception, and visual acuity. The human interpupillary distance (IPD)—the transverse Euclidean distance between the optical centers of the pupils—ranges from 51 mm to 75 mm across 99% of the global adult population, with a global mean of 63 mm.

Translating the human pupil just 1.5 mm off the primary interpupillary optical axis causes the pancake optics Modulation Transfer Function (MTF) to drop by over 45%, introducing severe astigmatic blur, chromatic fringing, and geometric coma aberrations. To eliminate this entire error class, Apple eliminated manual mechanical dials, ratchets, and sliders entirely.

2. Actuator Selection: Voice Coil Motors vs. Stepper Lead Screws

Miniature stepper motors paired with lead screws—the standard industrial approach in camera zoom stages—suffer from mechanical backlash, acoustic resonance that conducts through the facial bones of the zygomatic arch, and grease outgassing.

Instead, Apple engineered custom miniature dual-gap voice coil motors (VCMs) mounted directly to the optical carriages and suspended on planar beryllium-copper flexure spring suspensions. Operating via the Lorentz force, the VCM produces completely smooth, frictionless linear translation in absolute acoustic silence with full-stroke position settling in under 120 milliseconds.

3. Closed-Loop Metrology: Sub-Micron Optical Linear Encoders

Apple developed custom reflective optical linear encoders integrated directly along the structural magnesium guide rail:

  • Photolithographic Chrome-on-Glass Scale: A precision glass encoder scale etched with reflective chrome lines at a 20-micron pitch runs parallel to the transverse carriage guide shaft.
  • 256x Digital Sub-Division: The dedicated encoder ASIC digitizes and interpolates analog quadrature sine waves down to 1/256th of a pitch period, resolving linear displacement down to 0.078 microns (78 nanometers).
